name: XLSX I/O (xlsxio)
baseline: openpyxl (read_only=True); also xlrd, sxl and xlsx2csv in the same table
workload: Read every row of a 100,000-row mixed-type .xlsx file (and a 100-row file) into a Python list, via the python-xlsxio Cython wrapper around the xlsxio C reader, versus pure-Python xlsx readers.
claimed_speedup: Big file (100000 rows), min of 3 runs: xlsxio with types 1.08584 s, without types 0.93787 s, without types all bytes 0.88268 s, versus openpyxl read-only 6.34512 s, xlrd 4.10823 s, sxl 4.9788 s, xlsx2csv 6.53466 s. Small file (100 rows): xlsxio 0.00128 s versus openpyxl 0.01131 s, xlrd 0.00486 s. About 5.8x faster than openpyxl and 3.8x faster than xlrd on the big file with types (derived from page data); about 7.2x versus openpyxl with untyped bytes (derived from page data).
compiler_and_flags: not stated; Cython extension built by pip (README says building from source with Cython gives about 5% more speed); Python and openpyxl/xlrd versions not stated
hardware: Linux 5.4.44-1-MANJARO x86_64 (kernel string only, no CPU model)
stars_or_usage: 525 stars (xlsxio); the benchmarking wrapper python-xlsxio has 9 stars
tradeoffs: Reader assumes a data table (first row headers, values only; formulas, layout and charts ignored); whole shared string table is loaded in memory; worksheet cells are streamed. Writer supports a single worksheet and inline strings only (no shared strings, no formulas or styling). Depends on expat and minizip or libzip (zlib). The xlsxio README itself carries no benchmark.
caveats: Evidence is not from xlsxio's own repo: the numbers measure the third-party python-xlsxio Cython wrapper (last commit 2022-01-23, wrapper author is not the xlsxio author) including Python object construction, against pure-Python libraries, so it shows C-versus-Python reading, not a C or C++ rival such as libxlsxwriter or OpenXLSX. Benchmark script (benchmark/benchmark.py) and generator (benchmark/generate_xlsx.py, files made with openpyxl) are public, but compiler flags, CPU model, Python version and library versions are not stated, and the machine was a 2020 Linux kernel, so tier C. The openpyxl run uses read_only mode and list(ws.iter_rows()); xlsxio reads values only, so cell objects and formatting work is not equal. No numeric comparison was found for the xlsxio writer, in its README, Changelog, issues, or other shootouts searched (ExcelBench does not include xlsxio). Ratios are computed from table rows, not quoted by the wrapper.
found_via: seed-record pass: https://github.com/fffaraz/awesome-cpp#Office Open XML; xlsxio README had no numbers; WebSearch 'xlsxio benchmark faster than libxlsxwriter OR openpyxl OR Apache POI' surfaced https://pypi.org/project/python-xlsxio/ whose README holds the table
